writingFormula.title: 4-Part Story Formula（萬用故事公式）
points: Use the simple past tense (e.g. went, saw, was).
This formula also works for: losing a school bag, losing a phone, losing a pet, missing the bus, getting lost in a shopping mall, having an accident.

sampleEssays.title: A Lost Wallet
sampleEssays.content:
Last Sunday, I went to the city centre by bus with my family. We got off the bus, and it drove away.

Then I realised that my wallet was missing. I looked in my bag and my pockets. It was not there. I had left it on the bus! I was very worried.

I went to the Lost and Found office to ask for help. A kind lady had my wallet. She gave it back to me.

I was very happy. I said, "Thank you!" After that, I always looked after my things carefully.

sampleEssays.title: A Lost Wallet
sampleEssays.content:
Last Sunday, I went to the city centre with my family. I wanted to take a bus home. When I arrived at the bus stop, I saw my bus, but I was too late. The bus left before I could get on it.

I was worried because I could not find my wallet. I looked in my school bag and my pockets, but it was not there. I thought I had lost it on the bus.

I went to the Lost and Found office and told a staff member about my wallet. Luckily, a kind person had found it and handed it in. The staff member gave it back to me.

I was very happy and thanked her. That day, I learned to take good care of my belongings.

sampleEssays.title: A Lesson Learnt
sampleEssays.content:
Last Sunday was a sunny day, so my family and I decided to visit the city centre. We hopped on Bus 12, chatting excitedly about our plans for the day.

When the bus reached our stop, we got off in a hurry. As the bus pulled away, I reached into my pocket and my heart sank. My wallet was gone! I searched my school bag frantically, but it was nowhere to be found. I must have dropped it on the bus.

Without wasting a second, we rushed to the Lost and Found office and asked for help. To my relief, a friendly staff member held up a brown wallet. "Is this yours?" she asked with a smile. An honest passenger had handed it in!

I thanked her again and again. That day, I learned to keep my belongings safe and never to be careless again.
